title_en: The pronoun on the end of a verb
q_en: Who or what was it done to?
not_yet: Verbs with weak letters in the middle (like “he saw”): later.
Two pronouns together on one verb: later.
Why the verb ends in ـَ here: just read it.

slides.head_en: Eight endings on the verb سَمِعَ
On a verb, the pronoun is the thing the verb was done to
slides.head_ar: الضَّمِيرُ بَعْدَ الْفِعْلِ هُوَ مَنْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ.

cards.def_en: the ending = what it is done to
on a verb: ـنِي · on a noun: ـي

slides.head_en: Look: she, I and the present tense
sents: The boy did not hear him.

slides.why: Wrong! “Me” on a verb is ـنِي: سَمِعَنِي (he heard me). The plain ـي is for nouns: كِتَابِي (my book).
slides.why_ar: خَطَأٌ! «أَنَا» مَعَ الْفِعْلِ ـنِي: سَمِعَنِي. وَ ـي لِلِاسْمِ: كِتَابِي.

can: I can read a verb with a pronoun on the end (كَتَبَهُ، سَمِعَهَا، سَأَلَنِي) and say who it means.
I can tell ـنِي on a verb from ـي on a noun.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِعْلًا فِي آخِرِهِ ضَمِيرٌ (كَتَبَهُ، سَمِعَهَا، سَأَلَنِي) وَأَقُولَ مَنْ يَعْنِي.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُفَرِّقَ بَيْنَ ـنِي عَلَى الْفِعْلِ وَ ـي عَلَى الِاسْمِ.

items.en: Ali says this means “he heard me”. Is the Arabic right?
items.model: No. On a verb “me” is ـنِي: سَمِعَنِي.

items.en: Sara says this means “my book”. Is she right?
items.model: No. On a noun “my” is ـي: كِتَابِي.

items.en: Omar says this means “he opened it the door”. Is it right?
items.model: No. ـهُ already stands for the door. Say فَتَحَهُ or فَتَحَ الْبَابَ.
